newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FOCUS - NAB lifts profit but feels vulnerable.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - NAB lifts profit but feels vulnerable.

text.p: Australia's biggest bank, National Australia Bank, on Thursday reported record half-year net earnings but said it felt vulnerable to foreign takeover.

Unveiling a A$1.14 billion profit for the six months ended March 31, managing director Don Argus suggested that a government freeze on mergers between the big local banks had exposed all of them to the threat of takeover.
He said NAB felt vulnerable.
"I certainly do, particularly when some of our friendly merchant banks from the Northern Hemisphere tell you that you're at the top of the 'Hit Parade'," Argus told reporters.
The most profitable of Australia's banks and ranked its top bank by KPMG management consultanty, NAB has been seen as a likely predator if big bank mergers in Australia are approved.
But the freeze remains despite an official inquiry into the Australian financial system recommending that the big banks as well as major life offices be allowed to merge.
The government responded in April by initially declaring its ban on big-bank mergers would stay until it was satisfied competition had spread from home loans to business lending.
Argus criticised the government's position, warning competition was unrelenting and would put the group's ability to deliver further record profits.
The warning sparked sell orders on NAB shares, which fell sharply but held above A$18, a historically high.
At 3.10 p.m. 0510 GMT, NAB shares were trading at A$18.05, 29 cents down on Wednesday's close but off the day's low.
"Most of the comments that are accompanying the bank results are highlighting the difficulties with maintaining the same sorts of growth," said John Bowie Wilson, of BNP Equities.
On Wednesday, Sydney-based major Westpac Banking Corp reported a 13 percent jump in half-year profit but warned it would be hard to do the same again in the second half.
Argus said NAB would feel the impact of recent interest rate cuts in its second half, ending September 30, but thought the bank could match last year's second half result.
"We would like to think we could," he said.

If so, NAB would achieve a record annual net profit of about A$2.24 billion, just under state-owned telecommunication carrier Teltra's Australian record profit of A$2.3 billion in 1995/96 (July/June).
Before Thursday, banking analysts had forecast NAB to report annual net profit of between A$2.23 billion and A$2.47 billion.
But NAB will look for some upturn in the Australian economy to the second half-year to help it absorb cuts of up to 70 basis points on local interest rates it implemented in April.
"There will be an impact. There won't be any doubt about that," Argus said.

The most diversified of the Australian banks, NAB reported earnings growth across offshore operations: Clydesdale Bank in Scotland, Yorkshire Bank in England, Northern Bank in Northern Ireland, Michigan National Bank and Bank of New Zealand.
Even Asia, a small part of NAB's portfolio of markets, has begun to "put its head up now with some decent black figures", Argus said.
Net profit from the Asian business more than doubled to A$15 million from A$6 million a year ago.
-- Melbourne bureau 613-9286-1421
